semantic_changes: New harness file: a three-node in-memory cluster with the feature enabled, a user snapshot on one follower, 250 further committed entries, a graceful shutdown of that follower and two restart attempts from its own stores.
The stalled restart uses MaxAppendEntries 1 so 251 entries above the snapshot need 251 batches, and the control restart uses the same stores with the feature off.

scope.description: Live three-node cluster (A, B, C; in-memory transports and stores; timeouts scaled to 50ms) in which node A runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, is snapshotted early at index 6, receives 250 further committed entries so its staged commit index is 257, is shut down while B and C retain a quorum, and is then restarted twice from its own stores: once with the feature and MaxAppendEntries 1, once with the feature off.
assumptions: Every state that matters is produced by normal operations: bootstrap {A,B,C} from A, leader election with leadership transferred to B if needed, committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, further committed applies, and a graceful Shutdown of A.

The feature is enabled on all three nodes during the first life, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; this is what makes the commit-tracking store hold a persisted commit index for A.
A's snapshot index stays at 6 because SnapshotInterval is 10 minutes and the harness takes no further snapshot on A, so the replay must cover 251 entries.
Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; the control uses the same stores with the feature off so fixture size, store speed and cluster state are excluded as causes.
The stalled constructor is abandoned; a fresh transport is created for each restart attempt and the peers are reconnected to it.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or process kill is exercised; A is shut down gracefully.
The stalled instance is not resumed and no application-level timeout or supervision is modelled.

basis.prefix: The harness builds three InmemTransports (A, B, C) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); it bootstraps {A,B,C} from A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, starts A, B and C with MockFSM, waits for a leader and transfers leadership to B if another node won. It applies five commands on the leader, waits until A's applied index is at least four, then takes a user snapshot on A (index 6). It applies 250 further commands, waits until A's log store reports a staged commit index of at least 156, and emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the staged commit index, A's log last index, the number of entries the replay would cover, whether that exceeds the 128-slot channel, the cluster ids and the leader. It shuts A down, confirms the other two nodes still have a leader, and emits 'cluster_status' with whether the cluster is alive without A and whether the stalled restart returned. Each restart attempt creates a fresh transport for A, reconnects the peers, and calls NewRaft in a goroutine with a bounded window: 'stalled_restart' uses Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and MaxAppendEntries 1, 'control_restart' uses the same stores with the feature off. A 'control_restart_summary' event records the control's return and applied index. Event order: fixture, stalled_restart, cluster_status, control_restart, control_restart_summary.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft startup path: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays committed entries through processLogs into fsmMutateCh before the constructor starts the only consumer, runFSM.

comparisons.description: A follower restarted with the feature over 251 committed entries should finish NewRaft within the observation window.
Control: the same stores restarted without the feature should construct normally.
Control operand: without the replay the FSM stays at the snapshot index, so the difference is the replay and not the gap itself.
The remaining two voters keep a quorum while the restarted node cannot start, so the stall is not a cluster-wide outage in this size.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft cannot return when the replay needs more batches than the 128-slot fsmMutateCh holds

semantic_changes: Construct events now carry local_id in addition to mode, so their admissions can be correlated.
A second case pair with MaxAppendEntries=1 and 200 committed entries above the snapshot is added, with an off control at the same scale, so the trigger no longer depends on an entry gap above 8192.

before.description: One node (LocalID A) constructed in four configurations from per-mode in-memory stores: a version-1 snapshot at index 1000 with configuration {A} plus committed LogCommand entries above it, with the commit-tracking store reporting the log's last index as commit index. Cases: 9000 entries with default MaxAppendEntries 64, feature off and on; 200 entries with MaxAppendEntries 1, feature off and on.
assumptions: The fixture (snapshot, entries, staged commit index) is supplied by the harness; it is the restart shape a node that ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can reach, with the commit index persisted atomically with the entries by the store contract.
Batches are derived as ceil(entries above the snapshot / MaxAppendEntries) and emitted as an operand rather than asserted from a constant.

Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; each feature-on case has a feature-off control over the identical fixture and store objects, so fixture size, store speed and FSM speed are excluded as causes.
The feature-on instance that does not return cannot be shut down; its goroutine is abandoned when the test process exits.
excluded: No on-disk store, no live cluster and no crash path is exercised.
The stalled constructor is not resumed and no timeout or external supervision is modelled.

prefix.before: Per case the harness builds fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); writes a version-1 snapshot at index 1000, term 1 with configuration {A} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; stores the case's LogCommand entries at indices 1001.. in batches of 256; and calls logs.StageCommitIndex(last index). It emits a 'fixture' event with the case operands (mode, snapshot index, log last index, stored commit index, entries above the snapshot, MaxAppendEntries, batches required, observation window), then builds Config from DefaultConfig() with LocalID "A", the case's MaxAppendEntries, a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs from the case, and calls NewRaft(conf, probeFSM, logs, stable, snaps, trans) in a goroutine. A 'construct' event reports mode, local_id, newraft_returned and, when the constructor returned, last applied index, queued FSM batches and the observed FSM mutation channel capacity. Case order is replay_off, replay_on, replay_off_small_batches, replay_on_small_batches, so the event order is fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, construct; the probe FSM discards applied entries and accepts the snapshot bytes.

before.description: With the replay enabled over 141 batches, construction should return within the observation window.
Control: the identical 9000-entry fixture with the feature off should construct normally.
Control operand: without the replay the FSM is not advanced past the snapshot, so the comparison concerns the replay rather than the fixture.
With the replay enabled and MaxAppendEntries 1, 200 entries already exceed the 128-slot channel; construction should still return within the window.
Control at the same scale: the 200-entry MaxAppendEntries=1 fixture with the feature off should construct normally.

revision_reason: Reaches the same stall through ordinary cluster operations rather than a harness-supplied fixture: a follower accumulates a staged commit index far above its last snapshot by running with the feature and then restarting with a small MaxAppendEntries; the comparison set is limited to the new scenario's predicates and the earlier predicates remain with their own receipts.
